findings.where: Article specimen: the title "The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law", and "the world's best PPP law" in the closing paragraph
findings.fault: These apostrophes look straight (typewriter marks). The rest of the sheet uses curly quotes: the subhead's ‘chapter topics’, the download title's ‘Abundance’, and "Mark’s" in the captions. So like marks are set two ways, and the straight one sits in the largest serif line on the article page.
findings.who_objects: Mark, a lawyer used to well-set briefs and journals, and any careful reader. A typewriter apostrophe in a display serif headline looks unedited, which works against the legal-journal polish this direction is going for. Angélique also needs it fixed, because her pasted titles will carry straight quotes unless the site sets them right.
